newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Straddles swapped in NatWest and Barclays.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Straddles swapped in NatWest and Barclays.

text.p: An attempt to take advantage of potentially differing volatilities was behind the main stock option trades concerning UK banks on Wednesday, dealers said.
It concerned selling straddles in National Westminster Bank -- with an expectation that volatility in NatWest would decline -- in order to help buy straddles in Barclays.
The deal involved selling 2,700 January 700 calls at 36p in NatWest as well as 2,700 January 700 puts at 26p. In Barclays, 2,000 April 950 puts and calls at 54p and 55p were each bought.
By 1340 GMT, NatWest shares up 7p to 699p while those of Barclays were down 3-1/2p to 946p.

Over in mobile phone company Vodafone the main deal was the sale of 660 November 220 puts at 5p which may have been struck in the belief the shares will stay above 220p at expiry in order to collect the maximum 5p profit.

Vodafone shares added 3-1/2p to 225p. On Tuesday, the company said it gained 185,000 net new worldwide subscribers in the third quarter -- a rise of 31 percent -- bringing its subscriber base to nearly 3.5 million.
A short straddle was the chief deal in British Gas and it involved selling 250 December 200 puts and calls at 5-1/2p and 10-1/2p each making a net credit of 16p.
In the European style FTSE 100 index a popular strategy was to trade strangles. A number of deals were struck totalling 4,500 puts and calls in the same options series.

Traders either bought or sold the September 3425 puts at prices around 46p as well as the September 4525 calls at around 55p. The biggest deal was from a buyer of 1,000 puts and calls who will make money if the FTSE either goes below 3,324 or it goes above 4,626 by the expiry date in September 1997.
By 1340 GMT, the FTSE was up 20.9 points at 4013.1.
